title: The Earthquake
text:
In March, a strong earthquake shook a small town in Japan. The ground moved for almost one minute, and many buildings fell down. Fortunately, the people in the town knew what to do because they practised every year.

After the earthquake, the emergency team arrived in two hours. They brought water, food, and blankets to the families. Many people stayed in a school for a few nights until their homes were safe.

questions.text: How long did the emergency team take to arrive?
What can you infer about the town's preparation for earthquakes?
options: It had no plan at all.
It was well prepared for earthquakes.
It had never felt an earthquake.
It had stopped doing drills years ago.

questions.text: Why did many people stay in the school?
options: Their homes were not safe yet.
They wanted to learn in class.
The school was a holiday camp.
They were on a school trip.

vocabulary.definition: a sudden, strong shaking of the ground
a serious situation that needs quick action
thick covers used to keep warm

paragraph_translations: En marzo, un fuerte terremoto sacudió una pequeña ciudad de Japón. El suelo se movió durante casi un minuto, y muchos edificios se derrumbaron. Afortunadamente, la gente de la ciudad sabía qué hacer porque practicaba cada año.

Después del terremoto, el equipo de emergencia llegó en dos horas. Llevó agua, comida y mantas a las familias. Muchas personas se quedaron en una escuela durante unas noches hasta que sus casas estuvieron seguras.
